resources.string: your LLM, close to you — never in the cloud
VicinoLLM runs a local OpenAI-compatible HTTP server on this device. Point any OpenAI-compatible client at http://<phone-ip>:8080/v1 — the chat stays on your LAN.
VicinoLLM is free. If it\'s useful to you, a small tip keeps development going.

VicinoLLM itself is released under the Apache License 2.0. It depends on LiteRT-LM (Apache 2.0), Ktor (Apache 2.0), Material Components (Apache 2.0), highlight.js (BSD-3), and AndroidX libraries (Apache 2.0).
Model files (*.litertlm) are not bundled. You download them yourself and the upstream license applies — Gemma Terms of Use forbid paid hosted-inference services, so VicinoLLM is free by design.
Default GPU. Switch to CPU if the Mali driver on the S10 crashes or outputs garbage.
Auto-restore last model + start server on app launch
⚠︎ Auto-restore was paused: the last model was killed repeatedly for memory pressure. Switch to a smaller model (e.g. Gemma 4 E2B) and toggle auto-restore off/on to re-enable.
Required to download gated models like Gemma. Get one at huggingface.co/settings/tokens.
If set, clients must send Authorization: Bearer <key>. Leave empty to keep the server open on LAN.
Optional. When set, the web UI shows a 🌐 toggle that augments replies with live search results. Prefer a self-hosted instance — public ones can see every query.
Asks the model to turn your message into tight search keywords first (+1–2 s per request, but much better results).

Heavy model on a tight-RAM device

%1$s is a large model (>2.5 GB) and your device has less than 12 GB of RAM. Samsung OneUI and similar aggressive memory managers are likely to kill the server during inference, putting the app in a restart loop.

The smaller Gemma 4 E2B model is usually a better fit — similar quality, roughly 1/3 the RAM footprint.

Proceed anyway?
Fallback values when a client request doesn\'t include the field.
Applied at model load. Larger = more KV cache RAM. Reload model to change.
How creative vs predictable. 0 = always the most likely word (deterministic). 1 = balanced. 2 = very random, can ramble. Start at 0.8.
Nucleus sampling. Keeps only the smallest set of words whose combined probability ≥ P. Lower = safer, more on-topic. 0.95 is a healthy default.
Sample only from the K most-likely words at each step. Lower K = more focused, less variety. 40 is a healthy default.
Cap on the length of each REPLY. Hit it and the model stops mid-sentence with finish_reason=length. Keeps runaway replies short.
Size of the model\'s working memory (KV cache). Includes full chat history. Larger = longer memory but more RAM. Applied at model LOAD — reload after change.
Context window applied at model load. Reload the model to take effect.
Test prompt (tries the engine directly, bypasses HTTP)

Notification permission denied — persistent notification will be suppressed.
VicinoLLM needs a few permissions to run reliably. Grant the critical ones to avoid the server being killed in the background.
All critical permissions granted. You can close this screen.
Required on Android 13+ so the foreground service can show its persistent notification. Without it the OS will not let the server keep running in the background.
Samsung aggressively kills foreground services for "memory pressure". Adding VicinoLLM to the battery-optimization whitelist is what keeps the LLM server alive on OneUI.
Optional. Lets VicinoLLM read *.litertlm models from /sdcard/Models/. Without it the app falls back to its private /Android/data/com.sectl.litertlm.server/files/ folder.
Some permissions are missing — the server may be unreliable until you grant them.
